shutdown_safety.label: REAL
shutdown_safety.method: source read (third_party/llama.cpp/vendor/cpp-httplib/httplib.cpp, Server::listen_internal()/ThreadPool::shutdown()) plus a real empirical SIGTERM-during-generation test
shutdown_safety.finding: membrane_server_run()'s listener.join() transitively waits for cpp-httplib's own worker-pool shutdown, which joins every in-flight request-handler thread (streaming and non-streaming) BEFORE returning -- so the post-shutdown membrane_model_close() calls can never race an active generation. Confirmed empirically: SIGTERM sent 1.5s into a real ~400-token non-streaming generation; the process stayed parked in futex_do_wait (verified via /proc/<pid>/wchan) for the full ~20s the generation actually took, then exited cleanly the instant it finished. No crash, no corruption.
shutdown_safety.disclosed_asymmetry: the non-streaming path has no cancellation signal wired to server shutdown (unlike streaming, whose stream_release() sets cancel_flag before joining) -- SIGTERM during a long non-streaming generation waits for it to finish naturally (bounded by max_tokens) rather than cancelling it early. Bounded, not a hang/deadlock, but a real, disclosed shutdown-latency asymmetry between the two paths.
